Thresherium is a static, self-guided tool for artists, made by Sinaida Krivchenko. It runs entirely in the visitor's browser as plain HTML, CSS and ES modules, with no build step, no framework and no external requests. It is available in English only. It has no accounts and no analytics, sets no cookies for tracking and collects no data: the only thing it may store is one line recording a storage choice, in the visitor's own browser.

How it works: one energy rating and eight questions place the visitor on three scales, drained, flooded or dry. Drained leads to a picker of eight short body practices (breath, move, ground). Flooded leads to one triage of everything in the head, sorted by impact and effort. Dry leads to one of seven thinking methods: five whys, issue tree, answer first, pre-mortem, inversion, Scamper, working backwards. Every route ends in a short commitment and a printable plan.

Routes (hash based, all on the one page): #/welcome (start and consent), #/ (arrival), #/menu/drained, #/menu/dry, #/menu/after, #/flow/:id, #/energy, #/commit, #/plan, #/exit, #/about, #/privacy.

Privacy details: https://sinaida-space.github.io/thresherium/#/privacy
Source: https://github.com/sinaida-space/thresherium
